BI 348 and BI 351 are two different B-flat trios: Pan Classics 'Op. 1 No. 1, BI 348' has a variation slow movement, while Hungaroton's Op. 1 No. 1 (Allegro assai, Largo ma non troppo, Rondo; the entry's source) is BI 351 per Edition Silvertrust, which dates the six trios 1800 (Artaria 1801) against c. 1790 here. Aka should probably hold BI 351 only and the BI 348 set may be a separate work; unresolved

Same conflation: Hungaroton's E-flat trio (variations, Prestissimo finale, 26 min) matches the BI 344 set, not Pan Classics' BI 343 (Polonaise finale). Year unresolved

note: Rolla's Bianchi-Inzaghi numbers are tangled in IMSLP and on the Pan Classics album: two different B-flat/A/E-flat trio sets (BI 348/342/343 and BI 351/349/344) are merged in the Op. 1 trios, and the 1828 trios and the Op. 2 quartets share BI 410/405/397. Rinck's B-flat sonata is for violin, not flute (Deezer mislabels it). Rolla's BI 425 is primarily an oboe quartet.
